column3: “What manner of” renders ποταπὴν; BSB includes “And that is what we are!” with the critical text. “The reason … is that” recasts “because of this … because.”
BSB has “Christ” where the Greek has only “He” (φανερωθῇ).
BSB has “Christ” for ἐκεῖνος (“that one”).
Close to the Greek.
BSB follows the critical text with “sins” (no “our”); it has “Christ” for ἐκεῖνος (“that one”).
“Keeps on sinning” and “continues to sin” render the present tense of “sins” and “is sinning.”
“Deceive” renders “lead astray”; BSB has “Christ” for “that one.”
“From the very start” renders “from [the] beginning”; “has been sinning” renders the present “sins.”
“Refuses to practice sin” renders “does not practice sin”; BSB adds “God’s” before “seed.”
“Are distinguished from” renders “are manifest … and”; “nor is anyone” recasts “and he who.”
Close to the Greek.
BSB adds “Do not be like” and “Cain” in the question; “murdered” renders ἔσφαξεν (“slaughtered”).
BSB follows the critical text with “brothers” (no “my”). “So” renders Καὶ.
BSB follows the critical text with “the one who does not love” (no object); the Textus Receptus has “his brother.”
“Eternal life does not reside in a murderer” recasts “no murderer has eternal life abiding in him.”
“What love is” renders “love”; BSB has “Jesus” for ἐκεῖνος (“that one”).
“Earthly possessions” renders “the goods of the world”; “withholds his compassion” renders “closes his inner parts.”
“Speech” renders γλώσσῃ (“tongue”).
Close to the Greek.
BSB leaves the second ὅτι untranslated and adds “Even.”
Close to the Greek.
“We will receive” renders the present λαμβάνομεν.
“He commanded us” renders “He gave [the] commandment to us.”
BSB has “God” twice for “Him” and “He” in the first sentence.
